messages:
jess: Ran into ergonomic pain when mixing context cancellation + generator streaming in a sample app. The pattern `for gen.Next()` + ctx cancel feels error-prone.

omar: Can you show the snippet? Which behavior surprises you?

jess: Repro is simple: start generator with request context, then auth token refresh triggers reconnect mid-stream and the request context times out. Caller sees random errors or a panic on Close() in some runs.

jess: Snippet:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
gen, _ := client.Generator(ctx, model, nil)
for gen.Next() {
  out := gen.Value()
  fmt.Println(out.Text)
}
if err := gen.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("gen error: %v", err) }
if err := gen.Close(); err != nil { log.Printf("close err: %v", err) }
```

lina: Hmm. Two UX issues: 1) Close should be safe to call multiple times, 2) Next() should honor an external ctx. Right now Next() blocks and relies on internal handling that conflates auth-reconnect with user-cancel.

omar: Proposed fix: add `NextCtx(ctx)` (or `NextWithCtx`) so callers can pass the current context at each iteration and get a deterministic cancel signal. Also make Close() idempotent and return well-typed errors (ErrCanceled / ErrClosed).

jess: I like `NextCtx`. Example API: `ok := gen.NextCtx(ctx)` then check `if gen.Err() == context.Canceled { // handle }`.

lina: Also suggest small onboarding doc change: show pattern `done := make(chan struct{})` and a goroutine `go func(){ select { case <-ctx.Done(): gen.Close(); case <-done: } }()` is too heavy for quickstarts. Better to show `for gen.NextCtx(ctx) { ... }` and `defer gen.Close()` so close is automatic.

omar: I'll prototype a patch: make Close() idempotent (internal sync.Once) and add NextCtx with cancellation-aware behavior. Add unit tests that simulate auth refresh by forcing stream reconnects and ctx timeouts.

jess: Please also add a tiny sample to go-sdk-samples showing the recommended loop; our new onboarding doc should link to it. New users kept tripping on this in support.

ci-bot: build queued for branch: generator-nextctx-proposal — run 1/1

lina: One more thought: document the semantics clearly; e.g., NextCtx returns false on ctx cancel and Err() == context.Canceled. Keep server-side transient errors (like auth reconnect) surfaced as RetryableError so callers can decide to resume vs abort.

omar: Good call. I'll add error types: ErrRetryable, ErrCanceled, ErrClosed for clarity.

jess: Thanks — this would make onboarding much smoother. If you want, I can help write the onboarding snippet and a small integration test that hits the token refresh path.

omar: That'd be great, tag me on the PR. I'll add changelog entry and note in migration guide.
